messages:
Anya: quick sync 10m - options for management-plane handoff for Private/VPC onboarding: keep single central mgmt gateway vs per-customer mgmt clusters vs hybrid. Need decision criteria and a safe rollout plan.
Mike: tl;dr: central is operationally lean but larger blast radius; per-customer gives stronger isolation but multiplies infra and automation needs.
Sarah: from observability POV central is easiest (single trace pipeline, unified metrics). Per-customer needs either federated ingest or cross-account aggregation which is painful.
Joseph: hybrid thought: central gateway for discovery/bootstrap + lightweight per-customer controllers for policy and sensitive state. That reduces attack surface while keeping central ops simple.
Anya: specific failure cases to evaluate: 1) cert/key compromise, 2) reconciliation storms during cutover, 3) slow agents increasing API latency.
Mike: cert compromise: with per-customer CMKs + separate CA per customer you limit lateral movement. Central CA makes revocation fast but systemic if leaked. Ops cost: rotation automation must be rock-solid in either model.
Sarah: cutover reconcilers - if we flip traffic we risk double-writes and racey state. Need a read-only sync mode on new control plane, and last-writer-wins handshake for cutover transition.
Joseph: network constraints: some customers require fixed egress IPs for allowlists. Central NAT makes that easy; per-customer gives strongest src-ip preservation but costs more ENIs/NAT throughput.
Anya: compliance: customers asking for dedicated mgmt planes want separate KMS keys and audit trails. Can central still satisfy via per-tenant KMS keys + strict RBAC? Probably, but harder to prove isolation.
Mike: cost sketch: approx per-customer mgmt cluster = 3 small GPU nodes? (not GPUs, sorry, 3 t3-XL nodes) baseline for 100 customers ~3*100 = 300 nodes vs central cluster ~50 nodes. Ballpark x6 cost.
Sarah: telemetry note: if we keep central, we must ensure tenant-level scoping at ingress so logs/metrics/traces tag with tenant early and PII is scrubbed before any aggregation.
Joseph: ops playbook: propose these primitives: "bootstrap gateway" (central), "tenant controller" (optional), "shadow-sync" mechanism, and a cutover orchestrator that flips DNS/route and verifies health.
Anya: what does shadow-sync look like? minimal API set: tenants, endpoints, certificates, routing policy, quotas. Sync only these objects initially.
Mike: sample terraform fragment for per-tenant bootstrap (very rough):
```
resource "aws_ec2_instance" "tenant_mgmt" {
  count = var.tenant_count
  instance_type = "t3.medium"
  tags = { Name = "tenant-mgmt-${count.index}" }
}
```
This is just to show provisioning surface.
Sarah: monitoring/alerts: for central gateway we add per-tenant SLA burn metrics and per-tenant throttles so noisy neighbors get isolated without full cutover.
Joseph: migration strategy: 1) central default, 2) enable "shadow sync" for target tenant, 3) run validation (config parity) for X hours, 4) switch DNS to tenant mgmt plane, 5) monitor for 24h, rollback if health fails.
Anya: rollback hooks: must include route reversion, cert failover, and read-only lock on tenant controller to avoid drift. Also a post-mortem checklist.
Mike: security caveat: when DNS flips we must ensure client certs presented by agent match the new CA or we need intermediate cross-signed certs during overlap. That's nontrivial.
Sarah: cost/observability trade summary: central = lower cost, easier telemetry, harder isolation; per-tenant = higher cost, simpler compliance posture, harder telemetry aggregation. Hybrid gives middle ground but more orchestration logic.
Anya: decision preference (prelim): default to central mgmt gateway + on-demand tenant controllers for customers with strict isolation. Must deliver infra-as-code provisioning + documented cutover runbook.
Joseph: I'll take ownership of the shadow-sync proof-of-concept + cutover orchestrator spec.
Mike: I'll own cert overlap/cross-signing approach and rotation playbook.
Sarah: I'll draft the telemetry tagging schema and the queries for tenant SLAs/costs.
Anya: I'll produce RFC follow-up with rollout checklist and remediations. Planning rehearsal with one consenting customer.
sre-bot: alert: gateway-prod-0 latency spike at 14:03 UTC, increased p95 by 300ms for 7m. Noted for cutover planning.
infra-bot: ticket INFRA-5001 created for shadow-sync POC (https://go/infra/INFRA-5001).
Anya: linking notes: https://go/notes/mgmt-handoff-draft (WIP)
Mike: +1 to rehearsal. Can we schedule a "dry run" in staging next week?
Sarah: staging dry run ok for me, will prepare dashboards.
Anya: thanks all, will kick off RFC update.
